assumptions: no verification oracle: the server never observes accept/reject outcomes
no verification oracle: the server never observes accept/reject outcomes
veritas_pe.evaluation_keys: rotation keys only (no relinearisation, no row swap)
veritas_pe.forgery_bound: ~2/t ~ 2^-53.0 (estimate via polynomial identity lemma, degree<=2; paper Thm 2 §V-B requires a lambda-bit prime t, proof App. C)
veritas_pe.mask: VERITAS public mask: adapter built from official primitives only. Extends the official MulScalar (same public constant on every replica/component) to a per-slot vector. No secret-key material used.
veritas_pe.packing: native only: row-major stride = block size; block 64 (single ciphertext when n <= block)
veritas_pe.program_sharing: shared_across_row_blocks (public data reuse, same nature as BFV public masks)

basis: Lattigo preset: bfv.DefaultParams (incl. PN14QP438) documented as 'ensuring 128 bit security in the classic setting' (lattigo v2.2.1-0.20210923173451 bfv/params.go:92-93)

HomomorphicEncryption.org security standard (Albrecht et al., 2018), classical 128-bit table: N=2^14 allows log2(QP) <= 438 for a uniform ternary secret with sigma ~ 3.2; PN14QP438 has logQP = 438 (at the bound, includes the key-switching modulus P)
secret distribution: rlwe GenSecretKey = ternary with P(0)=P(+1)=P(-1)=1/3 (rlwe/keygen.go:61-62, ring/ring_sampler_ternary.go:20-23); error sigma = 3.2 (rlwe/params.go:27)
the plaintext modulus t does not enter the RLWE hardness estimate, so the PN14QP438-T54 profile (only T changed) keeps the same basis
he_security.estimator: lattice-estimator not run (not available offline in this environment); the claim rests on the standard table and the Lattigo preset documentation

profiles.lattigo_constraint: bfv.NewParameters requires t <= Q[0] (lattigo bfv/params.go:126-127); default EncodeUintMul (RingTToMul) additionally requires t below every q_i
profiles.name: PN14QP438-T54
profiles.note: PE T: same approach as the VERITAS application examples (BFV preset kept, only T enlarged). Largest PN14 prime (54-bit) satisfying the condition of the official examples, t < every Q prime. Not a value from the official examples. Forgery probability ≈2^-53 (estimate).
